messages:
maria: quick flag — canary rollout v2 routing at 10% is showing a weird sample ratio mismatch across segments, need eyes
kevin: which segments?
sandeep: i saw this too in the dashboards this morning, mobile-eu and enterprise-small are skewed
jess: is this SRM or just transient noise from low volume?
maria: SRM by chi2 p=0.018 for " + "mobile-eu (expected 10% assigned, observed 6.1%)
telemetry-bot: query: ```SELECT segment, COUNT(*) as assigned, SUM(is_variant) as variant FROM routing_logs WHERE period='2026-03-20' GROUP BY 1;```
telemetry-bot: result: mobile-eu 1240 assigned, variant 76 (6.1%) | enterprise-small 560 assigned, variant 48 (8.6%) | global-web 120k assigned, variant 11990 (9.99%)
kevin: small segments have high variance, but p<0.05 is annoying for our early-stop rules
alicia: could be hash assignment bias for certain customer ids — we rolled a change to assignment hashing yesterday (PR #4123)
maria: good call. Was hoping to avoid rollback, but we should investigate assignment hash first
sandeep: I'll rerun offline reweighting and estimate power under observed assignment. If power is <0.8 we can't call end-of-canary even with negative drift
kevin: please share the power calc code snippet you use so we can reproduce
sandeep: ```python
# quick bootstrap power
obs = pd.read_csv('routing_snapshot.csv')
obs['w'] = 1/obs['expected_prop']
# weighted difference-in-prop test
```
jess: product-side: we only want to block rollout if the primary safety metrics are impacted (error-rate, latency). If it's just assignment SRM with no metric delta maybe keep rolling but tighten guard
maria: Agree: hierarchy: if safety metrics (p50 latency, 5xx rate) degrade -> immediate rollback. If SRM w/o metric delta -> pause and investigate routing bug
alicia: assignment-PR touched salted hash ring, short-circuit path for enterprise accounts. Could produce under-assignment in small corp segment
kevin: proposal: hold canary at 10% for 24h, run reweighting + stratified power checks, add SRM alert for segment-level p<0.01, and create a dashboard tile showing assigned vs expected per segment
sandeep: i'll run reweight and simulated power within 2h and post results here
maria: also add a telemetry query to compare assigned by customer_id_hash mod N vs routing decision for last 48h — helps confirm deterministic bug
telemetry-bot: scheduled query created: routing.assignment_srm_check (every 5m) -> alert if any segment p<0.005 for 3 consecutive checks
deploy-bot: canary pause applied at 1891234600 by @maria :pause_face: (traffic frozen at 10%)
jess: thanks. if power remains >0.8 and no metric delta after reweighting, we can consider slow rollout to 25% with monitoring window 6h
alicia: i'll open a quick PR to revert the hash-change to a feature-flagged path so we can test without full rollback
kevin: long-term: we should add stratified assignment telemetry into the rollout console UI (per-stratum assigned vs expected, quick SRM check) — makes these decisions faster
maria: noted. for now: action items — (1) @sandeep run reweight + power, post numbers; (2) @alicia open revert/feature-flag PR; (3) @kevin add dashboard tile + short doc for on-call; (4) i'll keep canary paused and monitor safety metrics
sandeep: posting quick numbers: after reweighting, estimated effective N for mobile-eu = 310, power to detect d=3% = 0.42 (underpowered)
sandeep: for enterprise-small N=140, power d=5% = 0.35
maria: underpowered -> we cannot conclude. keep paused and do not early-stop
jess: product ack. hold and wait for fix, do not ship to more customers yet
alicia: PR opened: revert-hash-flag (link) — marking as hotfix candidate
kevin: i'll add the dashboard tile and a short runbook: "SRM during canary" with steps to pause, reweight, check power, revert if hash bug suspected
telemetry-bot: alert configured and will post to #incidents if triggered
maria: thanks all. we'll reconvene after the hotfix is validated and power improves
kevin: estimate: after revert and 24h aggregation, expected assignment per segment should match within 0.5% if this was hashing bug
jess: if after revert we still see SRM, next step is to investigate routing policy fallthroughs and quota overrides
maria: end plan logged. thx everyone :thumbsup:"
